bacterial_leaf_blight.symptoms: Water-soaked lesions turning yellow to greyish-white along leaf margins, expanding longitudinally with wavy margins.

organic_measures.name: Cow Dung Slurry / Neem Cake Application
organic_measures.method: Spray filtered cow dung slurry extract (20%) or fresh neem cake extract (5%) to induce systemic resistance.

organic_measures.name: Water Drainage
organic_measures.method: Drain standing water temporarily from affected paddies to curb bacterial circulation.

chemical_measures.name: Streptomycin Sulphate + Copper Oxychloride
chemical_measures.active_ingredient: Streptocycline 1 g / 10 L + COC 2.5 g / L
chemical_measures.safety_precautions: Wear PPE. Apply during early morning.

prevention_measures: Avoid excessive split application of nitrogen fertilizer during cloudy or rainy weather.
Use resistant cultivars (e.g., Improved Samba Mahsuri, IR64).
Clip seedling tips only with sanitized tools if required.
sources: ICAR-National Rice Research Institute (NRRI) Cuttack Advisory
IRRI Rice Knowledge Bank: Bacterial Blight

brown_spot.symptoms: Small oval to circular dark brown lesions with yellow halos distributed over the leaf surface and grain glumes.

organic_measures.name: Seed Biopriming with Trichoderma
organic_measures.method: Treat seeds with Trichoderma harzianum (10 g/kg seed) before nursery sowing.

organic_measures.name: Soil Nutrition Correction
organic_measures.method: Apply balanced potassium and organic farmyard manure (FYM) to remediate nutrient-deficient soils.

chemical_measures.name: Mancozeb 75% WP or Propiconazole 25% EC
chemical_measures.safety_precautions: Wear protective gear. Follow label safety instructions.

prevention_measures: Correct soil silicon and potassium deficiencies.
Ensure optimal water holding capacity in the paddy.
sources: ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research (IIRR) Hyderabad

leaf_blast.symptoms: Diamond-shaped or spindle-shaped lesions with grey or whitish centers and reddish-brown margins. Severe infections cause 'burned' canopy appearance.

organic_measures.name: Pseudomonas fluorescens Foliar Spray
organic_measures.method: Spray liquid formulation of Pseudomonas fluorescens (5 ml/L) at tillering and panicle emergence.

chemical_measures.name: Tricyclazole 75% WP or Isoprothiolane 40% EC
chemical_measures.safety_precautions: Apply at boot leaf / early heading. Observe pre-harvest interval.

prevention_measures: Avoid excessive basal or top-dressed nitrogen.
Ensure continuous shallow flooding in the paddy during susceptible stages.

leaf_scald.symptoms: Zonate bands with alternating light brown and dark brown chevron-like wavy stripes starting from leaf tips or edges.

organic_measures.name: Copper Oxychloride + Plant Vigor Spray
organic_measures.method: Foliar spray of copper oxychloride (2.5 g/L).

chemical_measures.name: Benomyl or Carbendazim + Mancozeb
chemical_measures.safety_precautions: Wear PPE. Apply when disease threshold is crossed.

prevention_measures: Avoid close planting in dense clusters.

sheath_blight.symptoms: Oval or greenish-grey spots on leaf sheaths near the water level, enlarging to irregular 'snake-skin' lesions with brown borders.

organic_measures.name: Trichoderma viride + Pseudomonas fluorescens Soil & Canopy Application
organic_measures.method: Apply bio-control consortium (1 kg/acre mixed with 50 kg farmyard manure).

chemical_measures.name: Hexaconazole 5% SC or Validamycin 3% L
chemical_measures.safety_precautions: Direct spray towards the lower stem and sheath region. Wear PPE.

prevention_measures: Skim floating sclerotial bodies during land preparation before transplanting.
Wider spacing (20x15 cm) to facilitate lower-canopy aeration.

healthy_rice_leaf.symptoms: Erect, clean green leaves, sturdy tillers, no sheath or leaf discoloration.

organic_measures.name: Azospirillum & Phosphobacteria Bio-fertilizer
organic_measures.method: Apply beneficial bio-fertilizers to support root nitrogen fixation and phosphorus solubilization.

prevention_measures: Maintain water depth according to growth stage.
sources: ICAR-NRRI Good Agronomic Practices for Rice
